topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
response: Interleaved array element spacing in Ka-band satellite links impacts coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression through frequency reuse.  Adjacent beams experience interference, leading to signal degradation as per SINR. To mitigate this, operators employ sub-bands with disjoint frequencies (as per Fig. 2) or orthogonal polarizations for beam separation.
reference_context: The Ka band's high versatility has led to deep architectural changes in satellite communication. Spot beams allow frequency reuse operation, leading to interbeam interference and SINR degradation. To mitigate this, operators use sub-bands with disjoint frequencies (as per Fig. 2) or orthogonal polarizations for beam separation.
